title: Agreement 3
note: Above a1_agreement / a2_agreement. Three groups that trip Czech speakers: everybody/everyone/nobody take a singular verb; news / information / advice are uncountable singular; people and police are plural. Czech policie is singular (*The police is coming) and noviny is plural (*The news are bad) - the interference runs both ways. Thickened 10 -> 25 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop): 15 new, five or six per group, including the questions (Is the news…? Does everybody…?) and the negatives (don't agree, was not correct) that the singular/plural choice also lands on. Rules applied this pass: A7 nobody / no one - the pair is declared in gen_senses.py and, because the canonicaliser is word-by-word and `no one` is two words, every nobody item also carries the `no one` wording in accepts; A4 two cleared by giving the Czech the demonstrative it really uses (tu odpoved, ty zpravy). The three that stand are all `the police`, where English forces the article and Czech policie takes neither an article nor a natural demonstrative - noted in DECISIONS.md under the A4 entry.

cards.title: Agreement 2
points: You already know that **he /** she / it takes the -s form.
These three groups are the ones where the verb does not follow the meaning.

cards.title: Words that look plural but are not
cards.title_cz: Slova, která vypadají množně, ale nejsou
points: These have no plural. You cannot say *an information* or *two advices*.

cards.title: Words that look singular but are not
cards.title_cz: Slova, která vypadají jednotně, ale nejsou
points: **police** is always plural in English, whatever Czech does.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Czech and English disagree about which of these are plural.

items.explanation: **everybody** takes a singular verb: knows.
items.explanation_cz: **everybody** má sloveso v jednotném čísle: knows.

items.explanation: **news** is uncountable and singular, in spite of the -s.
items.explanation_cz: **news** je nepočitatelné a jednotné, i když končí na -s.

items.explanation: **police** is always plural in English, even though Czech *policie* is singular.
items.explanation_cz: **police** je v angličtině vždycky množné, i když české *policie* je jednotné.

items.explanation: **nobody** is singular: was.
items.explanation_cz: **nobody** je jednotné: was.

items.explanation: **people** is a plural noun: are waiting.
items.explanation_cz: **people** je množné podstatné jméno: are waiting.

items.explanation: **information** is uncountable and singular: was.
items.explanation_cz: **information** je nepočitatelné a jednotné: was.

items.explanation: **everyone** is singular, so **has** finished.
items.explanation_cz: **everyone** je jednotné, takže **has** finished.

items.explanation: **advice** is uncountable: was, and never *advices*.
items.explanation_cz: **advice** je nepočitatelné: was, a nikdy *advices*.

items.explanation: **somebody** is singular: has taken.
items.explanation_cz: **somebody** je jednotné: has taken.

items.explanation: Plural **police** in the past: were.
items.explanation_cz: Množné **police** v minulém čase: were.

items.explanation: **everyone** is one group, so the verb is singular: **was**.
items.explanation_cz: **everyone** je jedna skupina, takže sloveso je v jednotném čísle: **was**.

items.explanation: **nobody** takes the -s form, exactly like *he*: nobody **knows**.
items.explanation_cz: **nobody** má tvar s -s, přesně jako *he*: nobody **knows**.

items.explanation: **someone** is singular: **is** waiting, never are.
items.explanation_cz: **someone** je jednotné číslo: **is** waiting, nikdy are.

items.explanation: The verb after **everybody** takes -s: **wants**, however many people you mean.
items.explanation_cz: Sloveso po **everybody** má -s: **wants**, ať máš na mysli kolik lidí chceš.

items.en: Nobody has seen him since Monday.
accepts: Nobody has seen him since Monday.
No one has seen him since Monday.
items.wrong: Nobody have seen him since Monday.
items.explanation: **nobody** is singular, so the auxiliary is **has**, not have.
items.explanation_cz: **nobody** je jednotné číslo, takže pomocné sloveso je **has**, ne have.

items.explanation: **information** has no plural and takes a singular verb: **is**.
items.explanation_cz: **information** nemá množné číslo a má sloveso v jednotném čísle: **is**.

items.explanation: One singular word, one singular verb: information **was not**.
items.explanation_cz: Jedno slovo v jednotném čísle, jedno sloveso v jednotném čísle: information **was not**.

items.en: His advice was not very good.
accepts: His advice was not very good.
items.wrong: His advices were not very good.
items.explanation: **advice** is uncountable — no *advices*, and the verb is **was**.
items.explanation_cz: **advice** je nepočitatelné — žádné *advices* a sloveso je **was**.

items.explanation: Even in a question, **news** is singular: **Is** the news…?
items.explanation_cz: I v otázce je **news** jednotné číslo: **Is** the news…?

items.explanation: *Zprávy* is plural in Czech, **news** is singular in English: **was**.
items.explanation_cz: *Zprávy* jsou česky množné číslo, **news** je anglicky jednotné: **was**.

items.cz: Lidé se mě na to často ptají.
items.explanation: **people** is plural, so no -s on the verb: people **ask**.
items.explanation_cz: **people** je množné číslo, takže na slovese není -s: people **ask**.

items.en: Young people are always on their phones.
items.cz: Mladí lidé jsou pořád na telefonu.
items.gap: Young people ____ always on their phones. (be)
accepts: Young people are always on their phones.
items.wrong: Young people is always on their phones.
items.explanation: **people** takes a plural verb: **are**. There is no *peoples* here either.
items.explanation_cz: **people** má sloveso v množném čísle: **are**. A žádné *peoples* tu není.

items.en: Most people don't agree with him.
accepts: Most people don't agree with him.
Most people do not agree with him.
items.wrong: Most people doesn't agree with him.
items.explanation: Plural **people** takes **don't**, not doesn't.
items.explanation_cz: Množné **people** má **don't**, ne doesn't.

items.en: The police have found my car.
accepts: The police have found my car.
items.wrong: The police has found my car.
items.explanation: **police** is plural in English, so the auxiliary is **have**, whatever Czech does.
items.explanation_cz: **police** je v angličtině množné číslo, takže pomocné sloveso je **have**, ať čeština dělá cokoli.

items.explanation: **everybody** is singular, so the question word is **Does**.
items.explanation_cz: **everybody** je jednotné číslo, takže se ptáme s **Does**.
